clue.text: Honest claim about bandit?

indicators.note: about can mean in a disordered state, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a one-armed bandit is a gambling machine, so the plain truth about it is a description of what it really is

explanation.surface: Someone vouches truthfully for an outlaw's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandit' suggests a robber, but a one-armed bandit is the slang name for a gambling device; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: One-armed bandit is the slang name for a coin-operated gambling device with a lever.

clue.text: Little box?

parts.note: box is a kind of tree, so a small young one is a juvenile tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container, but it is the shrub or tree used for hedging; a young one is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young tree, such as a juvenile box shrub, is called by this word.

clue.text: Topless broadcasting is due

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter of the down entry is cut off

parts.note: broadcasting seed by scattering it is sowing

explanation.surface: A notice that a topless broadcast is scheduled to air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests radio or TV, but here it is scattering seed: SOWING, with its top letter S removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still to be paid is described as outstanding or payable, which is what due means.

clue.text: Still produce nonsense

definitions.meaning: a still makes illicit spirit, bootleg whisky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb, but it is the distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg liquor and foolish talk are both known by this word.

clue.text: Cook revolutionary food for starter

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cook serves radical food as the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook in a professional kitchen is a synonym for this word.

clue.text: Extremely cool suit

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
spades is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: Praise for a very stylish outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning in great abundance or to a great degree.

clue.text: Pass a law bringing woman to court

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Legislators pass a statute so a woman can be taken to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a bill into statute is to make it legally binding, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Struggle to get a grip?

definitions.meaning: a ... literally takes hold of an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a grip' usually means calm down; here it is taken literally, as a grappler seizing an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with someone or with a problem is a synonym for struggling.

clue.text: Force detailed bugging US statesman

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its final letter docked

parts.note: something bugging you is rankling

explanation.surface: The armed forces planted bugs on an American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but it means losing a tail: RANKLING without its last G.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was a Founding Father of the United States and a diplomat.

clue.text: Leaderless miners confused with pros and cons

indicators.note: mixed up, so these letters are rearranged
without its leader, the opening letter of miners goes

explanation.surface: Miners without a leader are torn between arguments for and against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' drops M from miners, leaving INERS; 'confused' scrambles INERS with PROS. 'Pros and cons' looks like a set phrase, but 'cons' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Con is slang for convict, so cons are inmates of a jail.

clue.text: A grand on European match

parts.note: G is short for a grand, a thousand
re means on or about

explanation.surface: A thousand bet on a European football game.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond, which is the verb's sense of being consistent.

clue.text: At home, doctor gets drink

parts.note: someone in is at home

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor making a house call has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food or liquid is to take it in, so drinking is a form of this.

clue.text: Scorsese perhaps joining Spielberg film, 'The Disciplinarian'

parts.note: Martin Scorsese, the film director; Martin is his first name
E.T. is the 1982 Steven Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A film title made by combining two great directors' work.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict enforcer of rules is named after a famously harsh seventeenth-century French drillmaster.

clue.text: Some visit Argentina, returning for free

indicators.note: coming back, so the letters are read right to left
only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: Tourists making a trip to Argentina and coming home without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks SITARG from 'visit Argentina'; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for without charge, used in English to mean costing nothing.

clue.text: Article involved rioter at the front

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news piece about a rioter caught up at the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical term for forward-facing or placed before, the opposite of posterior.

clue.text: Seventies pop duo avoiding sand in northern town

indicators.note: steering clear of, so these letters are left out

parts.note: Peters and Lee were a British singing duo of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A pop duo from the seventies dodging the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Peters and Lee had a 1973 UK number one; drop SAND from PETERSANDLEE. Peterlee is a new town in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-war new town in County Durham in the north-east of England.

clue.text: Former drivers meeting worker could be lively

parts.note: ex means former
Uber is the ride-hailing company whose drivers are hired by app
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Ex-taxi drivers mixing with a colleague might be high-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' stands for UBER, the ride-hailing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and high spirits, a close synonym.

clue.text: Country's former leader wearing nothing? On the contrary!

definitions.note: Country is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: wearing puts one thing on another, here around it
reverses the surface order, so the leader wears the nothing rather than the other way

parts.note: David Cameron, former UK Prime Minister
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A former leader seen wearing nothing, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' would put CAMERON round nothing; 'On the contrary!' says O goes inside CAMERON instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A central African nation, west of Chad and the Central African Republic.

clue.text: Service stations might be here, incidentally

definitions.meaning: motorway service stations sit beside the road, literally next to the highway

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: roadside services are alongside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase used to introduce a remark in passing, meaning incidentally.

clue.text: Splits reported according to religious groups

indicators.note: reported means said, so the letters sound like these words spoken

parts.note: by means according to, and sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: A report that a population splits along religious lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts into two equal halves, a specific kind of splitting.

clue.text: One in five love a superfood

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: One fifth of people love a fashionable health food.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American seed crop rich in protein, marketed as a superfood.

clue.text: Email mentioned housing complaint

indicators.note: the words house, or contain, the letters

explanation.surface: An email that refers to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests a grievance, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: Famous swimmer crosses river going to 'The Queen' for drink

indicators.note: the swimmer goes across, around, the river

parts.note: Mark Spitz, seven-gold Olympic swimmer of 1972
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A celebrated swimmer crosses a river to see the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of white wine and soda water is this kind of drink.

clue.text: Head in charge of subject

parts.note: top means head

explanation.surface: The headteacher is responsible for a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' suggests a school subject, but it means the theme of a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme or matter under discussion, a synonym of subject.

clue.text: Traitorous person with support for the arts?

parts.note: an easel holds up a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: A double-crosser backed by arts funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support for the arts' sounds like funding, but it is a physical stand for paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneaky, untrustworthy person is called after the sly animal.

clue.text: Nick cleans top to bottom? The opposite

indicators.note: rather than moving top to bottom, the bottom letter goes to the top

parts.note: wipes means cleans

explanation.surface: A thief wipes things down thoroughly, top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' reverses the instruction: the last S of WIPES moves up to the top. Nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for stealing.

clue.text: Encounter with side heard to be on the way up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read backwards
heard means listened to, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a team is a side

explanation.surface: A meeting with the opposing team that sounds promising.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM spoken is TEEM; 'on the way up' turns TEEM round in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone or to come together, the same as an encounter.

clue.text: Chew piece of meat outside entrance to McDonald's

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Munching a cut of meat outside a fast-food restaurant door.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch noisily is to chew vigorously.

clue.text: On hand

definitions.meaning: a worker, especially a manual one

explanation.walkthrough: Two tiny words each define it: 'On' as working, 'hand' as a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means in operation; as a noun, a worker or agent.

clue.text: Part agreement to accommodate return of Italian trade union

indicators.note: to house, so the agreement takes the next letters inside

parts.note: consent means agreement

indicators.note: going back, so the letters of Italian's abbreviation are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Part of a pact lets the Italian trade union back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' applies only to the Italian abbreviation, not the trade union, which stays in reading order.
explanation.definitionFit: A component or element is one part of a whole.
